guarantee_statute: Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003 (amended 2022): lower of 100% of prior-year revenue receipts or 10% of GSDP

2023-24.off_budget_note: CAG SFAR 2023-24 §2.7.1: the State made NO disclosure of off-budget borrowing through KIIFB (₹20,041.52 cr) and KSSPL (₹12,900.62 cr) — ₹32,942.14 cr outstanding as on 31 Mar 2024. New off-budget borrowing in 2023-24 alone: ₹10,632.46 cr (KIIFB ₹5,803.86 + KSSPL ₹4,828.60). Counting it, liability/GSDP = 37.84% vs the 33.70% Kerala FRBM target. SEPARATELY, outstanding government guarantees were ₹62,868.15 cr (5.49% of GSDP; ceiling = lower of 100% revenue receipts or 10% GSDP). The State has challenged inclusion of KIIFB/KSSPL borrowing in its debt; matter pending before the Supreme Court (Dec 2024).
2023-24.source: CAG State Finances Audit Report, year 2023-24, Govt of Kerala (presented to Legislature; single-file report)

caveat: Off-budget borrowing = real debt the State is liable to repay, kept off the budget by routing through SPVs (KIIFB, KSSPL) — NOT part of the on-budget total, and (per CAG) not disclosed by the State. Guarantees are a separate contingent layer. Source: CAG SFAR. Inclusion in State debt is sub judice.
